board_content.text: z = a + ib: real and imaginary parts
$a=\operatorname{Re}(z)$ is the real part; $b=\operatorname{Im}(z)$ is the imaginary part.
$z$ is purely real if $b=0$; purely imaginary if $a=0$ and $b\neq 0$.
Order is undefined on $\mathbb{C}$: '$9+6i>3+2i$' is meaningless.
You may compare real numbers, and compare moduli, but never two non-real complex numbers with $<$ or $>$.

segments_english.text: Let's pin down the anatomy of a complex number precisely, because small definitional slips here cascade into every later subtopic.
The standard form is z equals a plus i b, where both a and b are real numbers. That's the crucial part: a and b themselves live on the real line.
We call a the real part, written Re of z, and b the imaginary part, written Im of z.
Now the classic trap. The imaginary part of z is b, a plain real number. It is not i b. The i is not part of the imaginary part; only the coefficient b is.
Two special cases: z is purely real when b is zero, and purely imaginary when a is zero but b is not zero.

And complex numbers sit at the top of the whole nesting: naturals inside wholes inside integers inside rationals inside reals inside complex. Every real number is already a complex number with b equal to zero.
One more crucial fact. Order does not exist on the complex numbers. Writing nine plus six i is greater than three plus two i is simply meaningless.
You can compare two real numbers, and you can compare their moduli, which are real. But you can never put a less-than or greater-than between two non-real complex numbers.

segments_hinglish.text: Complex number ki anatomy ko theek se pin karte hain, kyunki yahan chhoti definitional galtiyan har baad wale subtopic mein cascade karti hain.
Standard form hai z equals a plus i b, jahan a aur b dono real numbers hain. Yehi crucial baat hai: a aur b khud real line par rehte hain.
a ko hum real part kehte hain, likha Re of z, aur b ko imaginary part, likha Im of z.
Ab classic trap. z ka imaginary part hai b, ek plain real number. Ye i b nahi hai. i imaginary part ka hissa nahi hai; sirf coefficient b hai.
Do special cases: z purely real hai jab b zero ho, aur purely imaginary jab a zero ho par b zero na ho.

Aur complex numbers poore nesting ke top par baithte hain: naturals inside wholes inside integers inside rationals inside reals inside complex. Har real number pehle se hi ek complex number hai jiska b zero hai.
Ek aur crucial fact. Complex numbers par order exist hi nahi karta. Nine plus six i is greater than three plus two i likhna bilkul meaningless hai.
Aap do real numbers compare kar sakte ho, aur unke moduli compare kar sakte ho, jo real hain. Par do non-real complex numbers ke beech less-than ya greater-than kabhi nahi laga sakte.
